subject: general
question: What is the IUPAC name of an organic compound whose formula is (O2N)3C6H2OH, and used as an explosive, an antiseptic drug and a fixative?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2,4,6-trinitrophenol**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Picric acid**, also called **2,4,6-trinitrophenol,** pale yellow, odourless crystalline solid that has been used as a **military explosive,** as a **yellow dye**, and as an **antiseptic**. 
 
• Picric acid can be described as an organic compound whose formula is **(O₂N)₃C₆H₂OH** and the IUPAC name of this acid is 3C₆ **2,4,6-trinitrophenol (TNP)**. Due to its bitter taste, the name **"picric"** comes from the Greek word (pikros), which means "bitter." 
 
• In 1771, a British scientist named **Peter Woulfe** created picric acid by mixing indigo with nitric acid.
 
• Beginning in 1849, it was employed as a yellow dye, initially for silk.
 
• Picric acid was once highly valuable as an **explosive** and was first used as a bursting charge for shells by the French in 1886, under the name melinite.
 
• Picric acid was the most extensively utilized **military explosive** by the time of the Russo-Japanese War.
 
• Its very corrosive action on the metal surfaces of shells, on the other hand, was a drawback, and its use dropped after World War I.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **IUPAC-**

 
• Full Name- **The International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry**
 
• Founded: **1919**
 
• **Headquarters:** Research Triangle Park, North Carolina, **United States**
 
• **Work**- The International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC) is the world authority on **chemical nomenclature, terminology** (including the naming of new elements in the periodic table), standardized methods for measurement, atomic weights, and many other critically-evaluated data.
